APA 7 Reference List Generator

Fast tools that run in your browser. No login, no sign-up.

Everything runs in your browser. Your text and files are not uploaded to our servers. No account or login is needed.

How to use

  1. Choose the source type and the language of the reference, then fill in the authors, year, title and the other details shown for that type.
  2. Check the preview and the in-text citation, then press Add to list. Repeat for each source; the list is sorted alphabetically for you.
  3. Press Copy list to paste the formatted list, with italics, into your document, or Download to save it as a file you can open in Word or Google Docs.

About this tool

Create APA 7th edition references and a sorted reference list for journal articles, books, web pages and more. Choose the source type, fill in the details and add each reference to the list. The tool formats author names, dates, italics, edition, pages and DOIs, and also shows the in-text citation. It does not look up sources online, so check titles, proper nouns and capitalisation against your source.

Frequently asked questions

Which source types and which APA edition does it cover?

It follows the APA 7th edition. It covers journal, magazine and newspaper articles, books, book chapters and proceedings papers, web pages, reports, theses and dissertations, conference presentations and online videos. Other types, such as datasets, software or legal cases, are not included.

How do I type author names?

Type one author per line as "Family, Given", for example "Santoso, Budi". A line without a comma is read as "Given Family", so the last word becomes the family name, and a single word is kept as one name. Tick the organization box for group authors, and put suffixes such as Jr. after a second comma. With more than 20 authors the list follows the APA 7 rule: the first 19, an ellipsis, then the last author.

Does it find my source details online, and is the list saved?

No. You type the details yourself and everything is formatted in your browser. Nothing is looked up online, uploaded or saved, so the list disappears when you close or reload the page. Copy it or download it first.

How are capitalisation, DOIs and dates handled?

Titles stay exactly as you type them unless you tick sentence case, which lowercases words except the first word, words after a colon and acronyms; it cannot recognise proper nouns, so check them. DOIs are turned into https://doi.org/ links, and a range of pages gets an en dash. Month names and terms such as "n.d." follow the language you choose for the reference.

Will the italics and layout match my paper’s template?

Italics are kept when you paste into Word or Google Docs. The downloaded file uses the APA layout: hanging indent, double spacing and Times New Roman 12 pt. Some universities require their own template or font, so check your institution’s guide, and if you write in another language also check which terms it expects (for example "Dalam" instead of "In").

Is my data uploaded or stored?

No. The tool runs in your browser, so what you enter stays on your device and is not stored by us. The only exception is the standard server log kept by the hosting provider, described in the Privacy Policy.
